A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Que is an inhibitor of intestinal and hepetic DMEs, and DTs, and thus reduces CsA bioavailability in rats.
Que is able to inhibit the expression of intestinal CYP3A1 and CYP3A4 and hepatic CYP3A and CYP2C, as well as hepatic OATP1A2, OATP2B1 and OATP1C1.
Que is able to modulate intestinal and hepatic CYP3A1/2, OATP2B1, and OATP1 B2 expression, and thus the pharmacokinetic properties of CsA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Que can modulate the expression of intestinal and hepatal DMEs and transporters and that this modulation can be responsible for the observed changes in the pharmacokinetics profile of CsA.
the pharmacokinetic interaction between CsA and Que may be due to the overlapping inhibition of intestinal and hepatical DMEs and/or DTs.
the modulation of intestinal and/or hepatic DME and/or DTs is a potential strategy to reduce the bioavailabilities of drugs with low oral bioavailability, such as CsA, in rats.
